feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Kushner and Witkoff visit Ukraine with hopes of restarting peace talks with Russia
entry.summary: For the first time, Trump's top envoys take their peace push to Kyiv — after talks with Putin in Moscow.

entry.title: Former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine on efforts to strike a compromise with Russia
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel asks William Taylor, former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine, about efforts made by U.S. emissaries toward a compromise between Russia and Ukraine.

entry.title: Diesel prices soar as U.S. farmers preparing for harvest continue to feel squeezed
entry.summary: Diesel prices have spiked just in time for corn and soybean harvests. Farmers need the fuel to bring in the crops, and many were already hurting, but there are factors offsetting this latest setback.

entry.title: The copper peptide trend has gone from creams to injections — ahead of the science
entry.summary: The peptide is supposed to deliver flawless and firm skin, promote wound healing and other anti-aging effects. So what's the evidence behind GHK-Cu?

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Five people are dead after a cargo plane crash at Miami International Airport, Trump's top envoys go to Ukraine with hopes of restarting peace talks, Germany's far-right party wins landslide victory.

entry.title: Former crime reporter John Simpson shares why he decided to go to clown school
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with former crime reporter John Simpson about Simpson's decision to go to clown school.

entry.title: Strikes between U.S. and Iran continue as they vie for control of Strait of Hormuz
entry.summary: The U.S. and Iran traded strikes this weekend, raising tensions as Iran announced a new route in the Strait of Hormuz and President Trump claimed the U.S. controls the waterway.

entry.title: Rubio to visit 3 Latin American countries this week
entry.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio heads to Colombia, Peru and Ecuador as President Trump hails a shift to the right in regional politics and a new era of U.S. dominance.

entry.title: Labor unions nationwide are navigating the explosive growth of AI
entry.summary: Unions are trying to figure out where they stand on AI. While some are focused on greater protections for workers, the building trades unions are already reaping benefits from the data center boom.

entry.title: With the midterms fast approaching, campaign season begins
entry.summary: Labor Day marks the unofficial kickoff of the general election season as Republicans work to maintain control of the House and the Senate amid President Trump's unpopular second term.
